overall: Atlanta is off to a slow start this morning, with the running max holding flat at 73.4°F from 7:00 AM all the way through 9:05 AM — suggesting cloud cover, residual moisture, or limited early insolation has suppressed morning heating. The current warming velocity of +3.6°F/hr indicates active heating is now underway, and with dewpoints near 62.6°F and light winds, the airmass has moderate moisture that could cap afternoon heating somewhat.
forecast_obs_notes: There is notable model disagreement today: NBM (83.3°F) and ECMWF (84.7°F) cluster tightly together suggesting a mid-80s high, while GFS is a clear outlier at 90.3°F — a 7°F spread that warrants caution. max_temp_prediction: With the flat morning trend through 9 AM and the two most reliable short-range models (ECMWF and NBM) agreeing on the low-to-mid 80s, the most probable outcome is a daily high in the 84–86°F range. The GFS 90°F+ scenario cannot be ruled out if skies clear aggressively and heating accelerates, but the ensemble probability distribution heavily discounts that outcome. Confidence is moderate-low given the early stall in temperatures and wide model spread.
